issues.title: Theorem thm:sy item (3) and the results table mix the t-scaling (threshold 1) and the Polymath scaling (threshold 4) under one symbol
issues.location: Theorem thm:sy item (3), main.tex:318-320; also the 'Results in brief' table, main.tex:95,102; and items (1)-(2), main.tex:314-317
issues.analysis: Section 2 (main.tex:122) fixes the Polymath scaling u=4t for I_T, J_T, and the intro table is headed 'Ratios in the Polymath scaling, where the threshold is $4$'. In Theorem thm:sy, items (1)-(2) only hold if I_0 and J_T are taken in the t-coordinates of Song-Yue (the factors 10^192, 10^196 come from x=10^4 t; code/songyue_compare.py divides capped_check's u-scaled values by scale^2 4^48 and scale^2 4^49). Item (3) then writes $48J_T/I_0=1.000664921591$ (t-scaling) and in the same item $48J_T/I_T=4.0030988047$ and $48J_0/I_0=4.0036348167$ (Polymath scaling). Read with one normalisation, these give I_T/I_0 ~ 0.25 and J_T/J_0 ~ 0.25, whereas the files give I_T/I_0=0.999890305384 and J_T/J_0=0.999756438740 (compare_sy236.json). The numbers themselves are correct (rechecked exactly; the factor 4 between the two scalings is exact since I scales by 4^48 and J by 4^49), so only the presentation is wrong. The intro table row for the witness likewise gives the t-scaled 1.00066492 under the Polymath heading.
issues.suggested_fix: State once that in Theorem thm:sy I_0, J_T, I_T are in Song-Yue's t-coordinates (criterion threshold 1, their 2001/2000), and write item (3) consistently, e.g. '48J_T/I_0=1.000664921590... (t-scaling), i.e. 4.002659686363... with u=4t; 48J_T/I_T=4\cdot1.000774701187...=4.0030988047...' or add I_T/I_0=0.99989031 as the companion paper does. In the intro table give the Polymath value 4.0026597 (> 4.002) or relabel that row.

issues.title: The 3.99 ceiling of Proposition prop:ceiling was certified once, not twice; only the weaker sigma=4 ceiling was certified at both precisions
issues.quote: The certificate was obtained twice, at $5000$ and $6500$ bits with different
issues.analysis: runs/gram45_lemma91_D21.log (v0.8, the 5000-bit run per the companion paper paper/main.tex:1305-1308) records only 'CEILING sigma=4/1 ... True' and 'CEILING sigma=3985/1000 ... False'; no sigma=3.99 run. Only runs/gram45_lemma91_recheck.log (v0.9, 6500 bits, split 1:2) records 'CEILING sigma=3990/1000 ... True'. The companion paper itself says 'for $\sigma=4$ at $P=5000$ bits ... and again for $\sigma=4$ and $\sigma=3.99$ at $P=6500$ bits'. So the stated certificate (3.99 G_I - 45 G_J positive definite) was obtained once, and both runs load the same saved weights (/tmp/claude-0/w45_lemma91.pkl), so the second run repeats only the Schur-complement step, not the weight computation. The proposition is still supported by one certificate, but the sentence overstates the evidence. (The research-log headline 'ceiling 3.99 certified twice' has the same slip.)
issues.suggested_fix: Replace with: 'The ceiling sigma=4 was certified twice (5000 bits, halving blocks; 6500 bits, split 1:2), and sigma=3.99 once (6500 bits); both runs use the same exact weights.' Or rerun sigma=3.99 at a second precision or split before claiming two certificates.

issues.title: C_0 is never defined, and the hypothesis 'C_{m+1}<=C_m+g for all m' fails at m=0 under Song-Yue's convention B_0=0
issues.location: Proposition prop:fibre, main.tex:182; definition of T, main.tex:129; claim that all four cap sets satisfy the inequality, main.tex:153-155
issues.quote: If $C_{m+1}\le C_m+g$ for all $m$, then the fibre $\{t\ge0:(u',t)\in T\}$ is
issues.analysis: T is defined by s(u)<=C_{m(u)}, which uses C_0 for points with no coordinate above g, but only C_1,C_2,... are given. Song-Yue's support (songyue236_witness.json params: 'B_0 = 0, B_m = B for m >= 1') takes C_0=0. With C_0=0 the hypothesis at m=0 is C_1<=g, which fails for all four cap sets (e.g. 0.6>0.112, 1899/2500>91/1250). So the claim at main.tex:153-155 that all four cap sets satisfy it is false if m=0 counts. The conclusion still holds at m=0: s(u')=0, so every u' with empty large set is admissible and the fibre is [0,min(R,max(g,C_1))]. The proof's step 'this forces s(u')<C_{m(u')}' is not needed there. capped_exact.py asserts the inequality only for m>=1. No computed value is affected.
issues.suggested_fix: Set C_0:=0 (or note that s=0 when m=0), state the hypothesis for m>=1, and add one line to the proof covering m(u')=0.

issues.title: The Lean attributions overstate what Lean checks: Kintali's m-range in the pieces is not <=10, and the Lemma 9.1 caps are not Lean-checked
issues.analysis: (a) lean/TwinPrimes/Caps.lean kintali_large_count assumes l.sum<=1899 (the cap), so it bounds the large set of an admissible point only. The correction pieces also integrate over non-admissible u'. Replicating the piece enumeration of code/capped_exact.py (tasks(): (m,j) with (m+j)g below the relevant total) for k=48, g=91/1250 gives 126 J-pieces (matching the note's '126') with m up to 13 in Corr1 and up to 14 in the I correction. So 'the ranges of m ... that occur' is m<=14, not m<=10. The Stadlmann (m<=9, j<=3) and Table 3 Charton (m<=16, j<=6) ranges do match. (b) charton_caps_valid checks C_{m+1}<=C_m+g only for the Table 3 caps (chartonCap), and charton_extra_le_six assumes 777<=s, which excludes the Lemma 9.1 support (C_1=31/50=775/1250). 'Lean-checked for the caps of [Cha26]' therefore does not cover the caps used in Proposition prop:ceiling, and no Lean lemma states the inequality for Stadlmann's caps. (c) Prop. prop:fibre uses no counting lemma (it is general), contrary to main.tex:436. The evaluators enumerate the ranges themselves and assert the cap inequality at run time, so no number is affected.
issues.suggested_fix: Say that Lean bounds the large set of admissible points (m<=10 for Kintali), and that the pieces run up to m=14; or add a Lean lemma for the actual range. Restrict 'Lean-checked' at main.tex:154 to the Table 3 caps, and state that the Lemma 9.1 inequality (0.68-0.62=0.06<=41/625) is checked by hand and by the run-time assertion.

issues.title: Remarks overstate Proposition prop:ceiling: it bounds the best ratio in V, not the best attainable ratio
issues.location: Remark 'what would change the picture', main.tex:418-419; also main.tex:388-389
issues.quote: moves the best attainable ratio below $4$. Any revision of the analytic input
issues.analysis: Proposition prop:ceiling proves 45J_{T'}/I_{T'}<3.99 only for P in the fixed 846-dimensional space V. The supremum over all F on T' is not bounded below 4 anywhere in the note: the only general ceilings in the repository are dual-weight bounds near 4.13-4.14. So the Remark's 'best attainable ratio' is unsupported. Likewise 'cannot give their 4.00438, which must belong to the caps of Table 3' (main.tex:388-389) needs the authors' space B_21 to equal V. The note admits a few lines later that this has been checked only for dimension. The abstract is correctly restricted ('in an 846-dimensional space').
issues.suggested_fix: Change the Remark to 'moves the best ratio attainable in our 846-dimensional space below 3.99'. At main.tex:388-389 write 'cannot give their 4.00438 if their space is V' or 'presumably belongs to the caps of Table 3'.
